notes: Pure function: libgit2(old, Some(path), new, Some(path), None), then patch.to_buf(). No network, no filesystem, no clone on disk — old/new are two in-memory blobs (e.g. from ado::get_blob). Because the original tests assert substring containment (patch.contains(...)) rather than exact equality, expected is expressed as a 'containsAll' list of substrings the rendered patch must include, not a byte-identical string. A Phase 3 [Theory] should assert the same containment, not exact equality, unless the .NET diff renderer is verified to be byte-identical to libgit2's output.

cases.notes: Both old and new are given as the same path on both sides (libgit2(old, Some(path), new, Some(path), None)) — unified_patch always renders a same-path modify, never a rename; the implementation has no rename-diff code path.
old is an empty byte slice, representing a file that does not exist on the base side.
new is an empty byte slice, representing a file that does not exist on the target side (a delete's current).
